reviews.why: The September 30 checkpoint on Escondida's supervisors fired as anticipated: the union voted 95% to authorize a strike, adding a labor-driven delay on top of the regulatory clearance BHP still needs, and mandatory mediation (five to ten days) means the dispute stays open rather than resolved. Copper slid to a two-week low this week, but market write-ups attribute the move to a broad risk-off base-metals selloff and a fading tariff premium, not to any easing of the Escondida situation -- consistent with the view that the length of this disruption is not yet reflected in price.

sources.title: Supervisors at BHP's Escondida mine in Chile reject offer, paving the way for a strike
Copper Hits Two-Week Low as Escondida Workers Vote to Strike

no_new_call_note: We looked hard at China's halt on diesel and gasoline exports, which pushed Brent above $100 this week, but the resumption point is already public -- shipments could resume once the holiday ends on October 7, depending on Beijing rebuilding stock to a stated level -- so the same information the market used to move Friday's price is the information a new call would rest on, leaving no view meaningfully apart from what is already known. No new call this week.
